The scars of the protagonist's choices reverberate throughout the trilogy and the subsequent books as well. SOmeone else mentioned The Martian, which is a good example. It's definitely quite hard from a science perspective and the author clearly did a lot of research. But do you think people loved it because of the rigorous details about the Martian atmosphere, orbital mechanics, interplanetary communication etc.? Sure, that stuff is cool, but the story worked because the protagonist had a unique voice and the premise was very compelling. People wanted to see a regular dude survive extreme, hostile conditions using just his wits and resources. 

Another example on the other side of the spectrum - Hyperion. My all-time favourite sci-fi book and one of the greatest ever written. There's almost nothing hard about it. It's got wormhole travel, time-travel and a weird Lovecraftian monster that's more like some kind of demi-god. Didn't stop it from being an incredible story - because it focused on its characters and their journeys. 

SO my advice to you would be not worry so much about the nitty-gritty mechanics of science. Just write the story you want to write.
